description: The common direction of the regular-expression weakness: not a caller who writes the pattern, but a caller who feeds a long string to a pattern that backtracks. Two facts are needed at once and neither is a finding alone -- a quantified group with a quantifier inside it, and something a caller chose reaching it. The two negatives are each half: the same untrusted string against a linear pattern, and the dangerous pattern against a string nobody chose. Both spellings are here, because a language that reverses the operands writes the same weakness the other way round. The last route is not about patterns at all: it is a query built one statement at a time, which no part of the lowering handled.

expected.note: the pattern as the receiver, and written inside a negated condition -- which is where validation lives and which the frontend used to walk straight past
the spelling the language actually uses: JavaScript reverses the operands, so the subject is the receiver and the pattern is the argument

unrelated to patterns: `q += ...` is composition written as a statement, and it was handled by nothing -- not the expression lowering, which reads `+` and not `+=`, and not the assignment lowering, which reads `=`
